cards.verification_scope_basis: The limb quotes the York-Antwerp Rules 2016 and turns on the operative wording of Rules VI(a), VI(d), C and D. That is external legal authority asserted on the page, so it is not TECHNICAL_REASONING_ONLY, whose recorded meaning in this corpus is 'no external claim asserted beyond standard architecture'. It is not a class rule or an OEM specification, and YAR is a contractual code rather than a regulation in force, so the governed class is PRIMARY_AUTHORITY_REQUIRED, discharged against the CMI text itself.
original_asks: Explain how GA was applicable for ship ever given stuck in suez.
cards.q_text: General Average — Explain including act and procedure followed.
cards.missing_limb: The card defines the general average act, lists the Rule A elements and sets out the procedure, and its Casualty Anchor names Ever Given in one sentence - 'grounding and refloating operations led to a GA declaration and cargo interests providing GA security before cargo release'. It never works the Rule A elements through the Ever Given facts, never says which expenditure was the general average act as against the grounding, and never says what the Rules exclude.
cards.limb_sentence: The current answer lacks the worked application the examiner asked for - which act was the general average act, how each Rule A element is argued on these facts, that salvage expenditure is allowed by Rule VI(a) subject to (b)-(d) while Rule C bars delay and loss of market outright, and that Rule D keeps contribution alive irrespective of fault.

The Casualty Anchor already names the casualty and the GA security point, so the anchor sentence is NOT repeated; the limb is placed as a worked application that consumes the card's own Rule A list and Procedure list. currentness.basis: The register's conservative floor said no exposure. Independently re-inspected anyway, because currentness_required is a floor and not a ceiling. Two present-tense assertions were found and both were checked rather than assumed: that YAR 2016 is still the current edition of the York-Antwerp Rules (confirmed - the 2016 Rules were approved at the CMI Conference in New York in May 2016 and no later edition has been adopted), and that the Suez Canal Authority settlement terms remain undisclosed (confirmed - the vessel was released on 7 July 2021 under a settlement whose amount was never published). Deliberately excluded from the limb, as perishable or unsupportable: current litigation status, the final settlement figure, which party ultimately bore what proportion, the cause of the grounding, and any allocation of legal liability. Which YAR edition the Evergreen bills of lading actually incorporated is likewise not asserted; the limb is written so the Rule A analysis holds either way, Rule A being word-for-word identical in the 1994, 2004 and 2016 Rules.
triggers_found: current edition of the York-Antwerp Rules
continuing non-disclosure of the Suez Canal Authority settlement terms

authority: York-Antwerp Rules 2016 (CMI), Rule A.1 - 'There is a general average act when, and only when, any extraordinary sacrifice or expenditure is intentionally and reasonably made or incurred for the common safety for the purpose of preserving from peril the property involved in a common maritime adventure.' Identical wording in the 1994 and 2004 Rules, per the CMI tabular comparison of the three editions.

York-Antwerp Rules 2016 (CMI), Rule VI(a) - 'Expenditure incurred by the parties to the common maritime adventure in the nature of salvage, whether under contract or otherwise, shall be allowed in general average provided that the salvage operations were carried out for the purpose of preserving from peril the property involved in the common maritime adventure and subject to the provisions of paragraphs (b), (c) and (d).'

York-Antwerp Rules 2016 (CMI), Rule VI(d) - special compensation payable to a salvor under Article 14 of the International Convention on Salvage, 1989 to the extent specified in paragraph 4 of that Article, or under any other provision similar in substance such as SCOPIC, 'shall not be allowed in general average'.

York-Antwerp Rules 2016 (CMI), Rule C.1 and C.3 - only losses, damages or expenses which are the direct consequence of the general average act shall be allowed; and 'Demurrage, loss of market, and any loss or damage sustained or expense incurred by reason of delay, whether on the voyage or subsequently, and any indirect loss whatsoever, shall not be allowed as general average.'

York-Antwerp Rules 2016 (CMI), Rule D - rights to contribution in general average shall not be affected though the event which gave rise to the sacrifice or expenditure may have been due to the fault of one of the parties to the adventure, without prejudice to any remedies or defences on account of such fault.

Casualty facts: the Ever Given (owner Shoei Kisen Kaisha, operator Evergreen Marine) grounded across the Suez Canal on 23 March 2021 and was refloated on 29 March 2021 after dredging and a tug and salvage operation; the owner declared General Average shortly afterwards and Richards Hogg Lindley were appointed average adjusters; cargo was released only against an average guarantee from cargo underwriters, or a signed average bond or cash deposit, backed by the shipowner's lien.
cards.authority_note: Sources disagree on the exact date of the general average declaration - reports place it between 1 and 5 April 2021 - so the limb says 'shortly afterwards' rather than fixing a date that the evidence does not settle. The Suez Canal Authority's claim figure is likewise not stated: the reported initial claim varies between sources and was successively reduced before an undisclosed settlement, so only the existence and separateness of the claim are asserted. Whether the adjuster ultimately admitted any part of the SCA claim into the adjustment is not asserted in either direction.
claims_added: the grounding is not the general average act
